notes: Box score from the Heat's 137–117 win over the Detroit Pistons at Kaseya Center on Nov 14, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from Field Level Media (also via Yardbarker), the Sun Sentinel and the Detroit Free Press (both via Yahoo Sports), Hot Hot Hoops and The Standard. All 137 Miami points and all 117 Detroit points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (37–31–35–34 to 39–21–26–31) add up to both totals: 39–37 Detroit after one, 68–60 Miami at the half and 103–86 after three, matching Field Level Media. Team totals (fast-break points 28–11, threes 16 of 41 to 11 of 34, blocks 14–6, free throws 33 of 40 to 28 of 32, points in the paint 50–52) and the biggest leads (Miami 20, Detroit 4) are from Covers. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games: Miami 7–6 and fourth in the East, Detroit 8–4 and third, Houston 10–3.

Miami won its fourth straight and moved over .500 for the first time this season after an 0–4 start (Field Level Media; Sun Sentinel). Nine Heat players had a block, a franchise record (Sun Sentinel; the box score agrees), and the 14 blocks were a season high (Field Level Media). Antetokounmpo had 37 points against Cleveland on Friday (Covers box score, Nov 13), so 71 in two nights. Klay Thompson returned from a one-game absence with ankle soreness and was held to 5:57 in the first half by foul trouble (Sun Sentinel). Cade Cunningham scored 33 for Detroit two nights after a career-high 52 (Field Level Media). Miami hosts Houston on Monday, Nov 16 at 7:30 PM ET (site schedule; Sun Sentinel), and Detroit plays at San Antonio on Tuesday (Detroit Free Press).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Davion Mitchell's 3-pointer, the last of back-to-back-to-back threes by Antetokounmpo, Thompson and Mitchell that extended Miami's lead to 121–102 with under four minutes left (Detroit Free Press via Yahoo Sports; the Sun Sentinel has it as a 9–2 run after Detroit got within 112–100 at 5:22, and Field Level Media says the three threes came over a 57-second span). With the threes back to back, Mitchell's took it from 118–102 to 121–102. The exact clock isn't reported, so the scoreboard shows no time. The shot isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Davion Mitchell's listed 6-foot-0 and 202 pounds (RealGM), in Miami's home white with No. 45 (RealGM). No wingspan from a named source was found, so his arms are drawn to his height. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
